messages.author: 3801eca3e490bdb8
messages.subject: How to call stan_model in stan function?
parts:
Hi, All

I am new to Stan and I am still learning the stan program. I have a problem with using stan for simulation study. I have a model that I am going to test, and I will call it for 1000 times in the simulation. So I am using the stan_model() function to compile the model once, and then try to call the model in stan() function. Here comes my question, how can I do that?

my_model <- stan_model(*****)

fit_my_model <- stan(*****)

Thanks
Fukiko

messages.author: 484c91357ac83f6b
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] How to call stan_model in stan function?
parts:
What you need is the function sampling, like in

compiled <- stan_model("model.stan")

fit <- sampling(compiled, iter=iter, chains=., refresh=...,
               data=dataList, init_r=.5)

On Saturday, January 16, 2016 at 1:02:38 PM UTC-5, Fukiko Takamatsu wrote:
I am new to Stan and I am still learning the stan program. I have a problem with using stan for simulation study. I have a model that I am going to test, and I will call it for 1000 times in the simulation. So I am using the stan_model() function to compile the model once, and then try to call the model in stan() function. Here comes my question, how can I do that?

my_model <- stan_model(*****)

fit_my_model <- stan(*****)

Marco's answer is true, although it shouldn't matter. If you call stan() multiple times within the same R session (and assign the output to an object), it should not recompile the Stan program. Even across R sessions, this should work if you call rstan_options(auto_write = TRUE) as is suggested by the startup message. Another alternative is to pass the previous stanfit object to the fit argument of stan() rather than specifying a file or model_code.

Ben
